resources.string: Keeps the swap off anything in front of the face: food, hands, cups, a microphone, hair. Uses the XSeg model on the GPU or CPU.
Swaps only skin, eyes, brows, nose and lips (BiSeNet). Hair, ears and neck stay original.
Teeth, tongue and whatever is in the mouth stay as filmed. Best for eating and talking.
The lips also stay as filmed, so the whole mouth is the real one. Most natural while eating or with the mouth wide open; the lips are then the original person\'s, not the source face\'s.
The app closed unexpectedly last time, because of %1$s. If it happens again, try the Fast preset, 30 fps or a shorter trim, and share a bug report (Settings, About).
Your last video is reloaded and all your settings are kept. If the app closes again, try switching off Faster masks (Face Masker) or using 256 pixel boost for that video.
"%1$s" was stopped at %2$s of %3$s. Continue from where it stopped? The same video, trim and output settings are used.
"%1$s" is swapped up to %2$s of %3$s and can still be continued. Swapping this other video replaces it, and its swapped part is deleted. To keep it, cancel and tap Continue unfinished swap first.
Works out the masks on the graphics chip while the AI chip swaps the face, at the same time. Faster with the masks on, same result.

Videos only: skips work a frame does not need. The masks are reused while nothing moves in front of the face, the expression restorer runs around blinks and closed eyes, and "Keep original mouth inside" works only while the mouth is open. Faster, cooler, almost always the same result. Previews and photos always do everything.
Fast: quick and still good. 256 pixel boost, occlusion mask, skin-tone matching; no enhancer, expression restorer or mouth masks. Also set Output settings to 30 fps for 60 fps videos.

Sets everything for the most natural result: 512 pixel boost, occlusion mask, real mouth inside, skin-tone matching, expression restorer, face enhancer at half strength, head-turn fade, motion smoothing. Slower. Keeps your model, faces and output settings.
The swapped face takes the skin tone and lighting of the video, so it does not look pasted on.
Puts the original expression back on the swapped face: closed eyes, blinking, mouth shape. Uses the face editor models (download them in Settings, Models). Adds time per face.
Fade out on big head turns
When the head turns too far left, right, up or down for the swapper, the original face shows through smoothly instead of a stretched one.
Head turn where the fade begins. The swap is gone 20° later. Lower is safer, higher keeps more of the swap.
Video and Live: steadies the face alignment between frames and keeps motion-blurred faces swapped during fast movement.
Also looks for heads turned sideways or upside down (90°, 180°, 270°). Slower on frames without a face.
Hair (and hats) always stay as filmed, and the edge of the swap follows the real edges in the picture, so strands across the face never turn into dark streaks. Uses the face parser.
Blends the swapped face into the video\'s own skin at the edge, so there is no outline at the forehead, cheeks or jaw.
A face shown big in the frame is swapped at 1024 pixels instead of being stretched, so its edges stay clean. Takes longer on close-ups only.
Videos: the skin tone and the edge of the swap change gently from frame to frame instead of flickering.

Recommended settings are on: face parser with hair-aware and seamless edges, close-up detail, occlusion mask, real mouth inside, skin tone, expression restorer 80, enhancer 50, smoothing, 30 fps and 1080p for 4K. Change anything in the gear on face_swapper.

Each face can have up to 5 photos of the same person (front, left, right, up, down). They are combined into one likeness, and for every frame the photo whose head angle matches the video counts most. Assign faces to the people in a video on the Swap tab (Assign per person).

Best photos: sharp, well lit, nothing over the face. One straight on, one turned left, one turned right, then up and down. Or tap From a video and the app picks the best ones for you. Each photo says if something is wrong with it.

Photos of the same person are combined into one likeness. For every frame the photo whose head angle matches the face in the video counts most (turned left: your left-turned photo), blending smoothly as the head turns. Add one straight on, one turned left, one turned right, then up and down.
Best: sharp, well lit, nothing over the face; one straight on, one turned left, one turned right, then up and down.
This phone could not run the %1$s models, so the %2$s set is used instead.
With the lip syncer on, it drives the mouth and these sliders are ignored.
Each slider runs from -1 to 1. At 0 the face is unchanged.
Builds the GPU and CPU models in a way that needs less memory, for phones with 6 GB or less. Slightly slower.
It is on for this phone.

Use the mirror if Hugging Face is slow or blocked where you are.

While an eye is shut, its own lids and lashes stay as filmed, so they do not smear. Each eye on its own (winks too).
Swap turned faces with side photos
If this person has a photo turned the same way (Faces tab), a face turned sideways keeps the swap 15 degrees further round before fading.
